metadata.description: 9 realistic sales coaching scenarios with expert tool selections
metadata.test_approach: Use actual OllamaPromptService to match app behavior

scenarios.name: Deep skepticism from past failures
scenarios.transcript: I've been thinking about this extensively. We've had bad experiences with similar solutions in the past. The implementation was a nightmare and took months longer than promised. I'm just not convinced this time will be different.

expert_selection.reasoning: Multiple strong negatives ('bad experiences', 'nightmare', 'not convinced') + late stage (7) + deep skepticism = strongest defusal tool
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Remove pressure, acknowledge their concern without being defensive

scenarios.name: Team discussion stall tactic
scenarios.transcript: That's an interesting perspective on how to handle the situation. We'll need to discuss this with the broader team before making any decisions.

expert_selection.reasoning: Soft objection disguised as process. No strong emotion to label. Needs validation before exploring the real concern.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Validate the team process, then explore what the real hesitation is

scenarios.name: Emotional exhaustion from repeated failures
scenarios.transcript: Every solution we've tried has fallen short. The team is tired of false promises. I don't have the energy to go through another failed implementation.

expert_selection.reasoning: STRONG emotional exhaustion ('tired', 'no energy', 'every solution failed') at mid-stage = Labeling to validate intense emotions. Too early for Take Away.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Name and validate the strong emotional fatigue, show understanding

scenarios.name: Buying signal with implementation concern
scenarios.transcript: On one hand, I see the potential value. On the other hand, we're already stretched thin with current projects. I want to move forward but the timing feels off.

expert_selection.reasoning: BUYING SIGNAL in disguise! 'See value' + 'want to move forward' = they want to buy. 'Stretched thin' = implementation concern, NOT rejection. Mirror to explore the real concern.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Echo the concern to get them to elaborate on what 'stretched thin' means

scenarios.name: Executive buy-in with middle management concern
scenarios.transcript: The executive team has been pushing for innovation, but there's resistance from middle management who are comfortable with the status quo. Navigating that dynamic is tricky.

expert_selection.reasoning: STRONGEST BUYING SIGNAL YET! Decision makers (execs) WANT it. They're asking HOW to get team on board, not WHETHER to do it. Mirror to clarify, then use Calibrated Questions.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Echo 'status quo' to clarify what middle management is protecting

scenarios.name: Stuck progress - going in circles
scenarios.transcript: This is the third time we've had this conversation and I feel like we're going in circles. I'm starting to question if we're even aligned on what success looks like here.

expert_selection.reasoning: Frustration with lack of progress (NOT hostility). Take ownership with self-deprecating humor, then reset with Calibrated Questions.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Take ownership with humor ('I must be the world's worst consultant'), then reset the conversation

scenarios.name: Vague risk concern without specifics
scenarios.transcript: We're in a critical growth phase right now. Any disruption to our current operations could have significant downstream effects on our customer commitments.

expert_selection.reasoning: Too vague and generic. Need more information before addressing. Mirror 'critical growth?' to get specifics, or use Empathy Questions.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Echo the vague phrase to make them elaborate with specifics

scenarios.name: Enthusiasm with budget approval concern
scenarios.transcript: This is exactly what we've been looking for. The features align perfectly with our needs. My only concern is whether we can get executive approval given budget constraints this quarter.

expert_selection.reasoning: High enthusiasm but QUALIFICATION ISSUE - they need approval. Mirror 'budget constraints?' to understand, then use Calibrated Questions to reframe budget as ROI.
trigger_words: exactly what we've been looking for
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Echo 'budget constraints' to understand what that means specifically

scenarios.name: Soft rejection at late stage
scenarios.transcript: Let me take this back to the team and see what they think. We'll circle back once we've had a chance to digest everything and discuss internally.

expert_selection.reasoning: Late stage + stall tactic = soft rejection / BLACK SWAN. Label to call out the hidden concern: 'Sounds like you're not that excited.' Look for the real objection.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Call out the lack of enthusiasm to uncover the hidden concern

casual_conversation_scenarios.name: Casual rapport building - golf interest
casual_conversation_scenarios.transcript: Yeah, I got a new putter about a year ago and I think it's a good one. I'm probably just not very good yet. I struggle with my short game.

expert_selection.reasoning: Casual conversation, no objections. Mirror to build rapport and show interest. Echo 'short game' to keep them talking.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Echo the challenge they mentioned to show you're listening and build connection

casual_conversation_scenarios.name: Early discovery - problem exploration
casual_conversation_scenarios.transcript: We've been looking at different coaching options. Not sure exactly what would work best for our team yet.

expert_selection.reasoning: Discovery phase, no strong emotions. Use Empathy Questions to understand their world and what they're trying to solve.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Ask open-ended questions to understand their specific challenges and goals

casual_conversation_scenarios.name: Positive progress - solution interest
casual_conversation_scenarios.transcript: That makes sense. I like how you explained that. Tell me more about how that would work in our specific situation.

expert_selection.reasoning: Positive engagement and curiosity. Get buy-in before explaining more - make sure they're invested in understanding.
expert_selection.expected_prompt_pattern: Ask a question to get them to commit to exploring further before explaining

quality_criteria.prompt_must_be_specific: Generated coaching must reference actual words from transcript, not generic templates
quality_criteria.prompt_must_be_contextual: Must address the specific situation, not copy examples from instruction file
quality_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: Selected tool_id must match expert reasoning
